paragraphs: On Sunday morning, Lily, Tom, and Dad went to the train station. Aunt Sue was coming from Chiang Mai. The station was big and busy. "Which platform is her train?" asked Lily. "It is platform two," said Dad. "What time does it come?" asked Tom. "At ten o'clock," said Dad. Lily looked at the big clock on the wall. It was five to ten.

The train came into the station. Many passengers got off. "There is Aunt Sue!" said Lily. Aunt Sue wore a yellow dress, and she waved from the door of the train. "Lily! Tom!" she called. Lily ran to Aunt Sue, and Tom took her bag. "Hello, Aunt Sue," said Tom. "How was your trip?" "It was long, but I slept in the train," said Aunt Sue.

"Do we go home now?" asked Lily. "No," said Dad. "We go to the restaurant in the square instead." "Mom will meet us there." "I am hungry," said Tom. "Is it the restaurant with the green door?" asked Lily. "Yes, it is next to the library," said Dad. "They make very good noodles." Aunt Sue smiled. "I want to go out and see the town," she said.

They walked out of the station and across the square. The sun was hot in the square. Aunt Sue looked at the old buildings and smiled. Mom waited at the door of the restaurant. "Hello, Sue!" said Mom. "After lunch, I want to go shopping," said Aunt Sue. "I need a present for Grandma." "I can show you a shop near the river," said Lily. Everyone laughed and went into the restaurant.
